title: Rounds Along a Round Orbit
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, let $a\in S$, let $E$ be a set of optional states, and let $R$ be a round contract for $M$ with anchor $a$ and escape set $E$. Suppose $c$ starts in state $a$, the precondition holds at every orbit configuration with index $r<n$, and each round endpoint with $r+1<n$ returns to state $a$. Then for every $r<n$, the run from orbit configuration $r$ to orbit configuration $r+1$ is a round of duration prescribed by $R$, with endpoint in the anchor state or $E$, no halting, anchor, or escape state at strictly intermediate positive times, and all work-tape head positions within the coordinatewise bounds given by the minimum and maximum of the contract bounds at orbit indices below $n$ together with the head positions at orbit index $n$.
hypotheses_covered: The precondition holds at every orbit index $r<n$
Every round endpoint with $r+1<n$ has state $a$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape machine and let $R$ be a round contract with anchor $a$ and
escape set $E$. Suppose $c$ starts in state $a$, the round precondition holds at each
orbit configuration with index $r<n$, and each round endpoint with $r+1<n$ returns to
$a$. Then for every $r<n$, the transition from orbit configuration $r$ to orbit
configuration $r+1$ is a round: it starts at $a$, has positive duration given by the
contract, ends at the anchor or in $E$, and has no intermediate state in
$\{\text{halted},a\}\cup E$. Throughout that round, every work-head position lies in the
coordinatewise interval whose lower and upper bounds are the minima and maxima,
respectively, of the contract bounds at orbit indices below $n$ together with the head
positions at orbit index $n$.
